title: Travel: John Lennon – Toronto to Frankfurt | 1969
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono travelled from Toronto to Frankfurt on 5 June 1969.

The day began with an interview given to journalist Ellen Sander at the Windsor Arms Hotel in Toronto.

At around midday a limousine arrived to take the Lennons to Toronto International Airport for their 2pm immigration hearing. Their attorney Alan Mintz spoke to Canadian Department of Citizenship officials for around two hours, after which Lennon was permitted to apply for a visa extension to remain in Canada.

Lennon was hoping to remain in Canada while negotiations to secure a US visa continued, but he chose instead to return to England. He withdrew his application for permission to remain in Canada, and was released under bond, on condition that he and Ono left Canada that evening.

Lennon, Ono, and her daughter Kyoko left Toronto at 9pm. The flight was not direct, and required a stopover in Frankfurt, West Germany. They arrived in back the UK on 6 June.

Booked on Air Canada for the flight to London, we were transferred without explanation and with no chance of redress to a Frankfurt-bound plane. Our triumphant if brief victory over the Powers of Deportation only slightly dampened, we were now thoroughly deported by our commonwealth cousins to Germany, of all the old ‘enemy’ places.
Derek Taylor
Fifty Years Adrift
Page last updated: 12 February 2026
